es.L: Y se contaron los hombres de Israel, aparte de Benjamín, 400 000 hombres que sacaban espada; todos estos [eran] hombres de guerra.
es.B: Los hombres de Israel, sin contar a Benjamín, reclutaron 400 000 hombres armados de espada, todos ellos guerreros experimentados.
es.R: Israel, sin contar a Benjamín, tenía 400 000 soldados armados con espadas. Todos estaban entrenados para la guerra.

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Israël furent recensés, sans compter Benjamin : 400 000 hommes tirant l’épée ; tous ceux-là [étaient] des hommes de guerre.
fr.B: Les hommes d’Israël, sans compter Benjamin, recrutèrent 400 000 hommes armés de l’épée, tous des guerriers aguerris.
fr.R: Israël, sans compter Benjamin, avait 400 000 soldats armés d’épées. Ils étaient tous entraînés pour la guerre.

vi.L: Những người Y-sơ-ra-ên, không kể Bên-gia-min, điểm danh được 400.000 người cầm gươm; tất cả đều là chiến binh.
vi.B: Những người Y-sơ-ra-ên, không kể Bên-gia-min, huy động được 400.000 người cầm gươm, tất cả đều là những chiến binh lão luyện.
vi.R: Không kể Bên-gia-min, Y-sơ-ra-ên có 400.000 lính cầm gươm. Tất cả đều đã được huấn luyện để chiến đấu.

ko.L: 베냐민을 빼고 이스라엘 사람들이 소집한 칼을 빼는 사람은 사십만 명이었는데, 이들은 모두 전사였다.
ko.B: 베냐민을 빼고 이스라엘 사람들이 불러 모은 칼 찬 군사는 사십만 명이었고, 모두 싸움에 익숙한 사람들이었다.
ko.R: 베냐민을 빼고도 이스라엘에는 칼을 찬 군인이 사십만 명 있었다. 그들은 모두 전쟁을 위해 훈련받은 사람들이었다.

pt.L: E os homens de Israel foram contados, além de Benjamim: quatrocentos mil homens que puxavam [a] espada; todos estes [eram] homens de guerra.
pt.B: Os homens de Israel, sem contar Benjamim, convocaram quatrocentos mil homens armados de espada, todos eles guerreiros experientes.
pt.R: Israel, sem contar Benjamim, tinha quatrocentos mil soldados armados de espada. Todos eles eram treinados para a guerra.

decisions.choice: 400,000: the same number as verse 2
decisions.reason: The count agrees with the gathering at Mizpah (verse 2). On the size of the number see the note there. Against 26,700 Benjaminites, the tribes' army was about fifteen times larger.

decisions.choice: a man of war: a soldier, a fighting man
decisions.reason: The phrase names a trained, seasoned warrior (Joshua 17:1; 1 Samuel 16:18).

decisions.choice: the men of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the man of Israel", a collective for the army. Here and through the chapter English says "the men of Israel".

source.text: וַיָּקֻ֜מוּ וַיַּעֲל֣וּ בֵֽית־אֵל֮ וַיִּשְׁאֲל֣וּ בֵאלֹהִים֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ֚י יַעֲלֶה־לָּ֣נוּ בַתְּחִלָּ֔ה לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יְהוּדָ֥ה בַתְּחִלָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they arose and went up [to] Bethel and asked of God, and said [the] sons of Israel, Who will go up for us at the first to the battle with [the] sons of Benjamin? And said Yahweh, Judah at the first.

en.L: And they arose and went up to Bethel and asked God, and the sons of Israel said, "Who will go up for us first to the battle against the sons of Benjamin?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Judah first."
en.B: The Israelites set out and went up to Bethel, and they asked God, "Which of us should go up first to fight against the Benjaminites?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Judah is to go first."
en.R: The Israelites went up to Bethel and asked God for guidance. "Which tribe should go first to attack the men of Benjamin?" they asked. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Judah will go first."

sw.L: Nao wakaondoka, wakapanda Betheli, wakamwuliza Mungu, na wana wa Israeli wakasema, "Ni nani atakayetupandia kwanza vitani kupigana na wana wa Benyamini?" Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Yuda kwanza."
sw.B: Waisraeli waliondoka, wakapanda Betheli, wakamwuliza Mungu, "Ni yupi kati yetu atakayepanda kwanza kupigana na Wabenyamini?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Yuda atakwenda kwanza."
sw.R: Waisraeli walipanda Betheli, wakamwomba Mungu awaongoze. Waliuliza, "Ni kabila gani litakalotangulia kuwashambulia watu wa Benyamini?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Yuda atatangulia."

es.L: Y se levantaron y subieron a Betel y consultaron a Dios, y dijeron los hijos de Israel: «¿Quién de nosotros subirá primero a la batalla contra los hijos de Benjamín?». Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «Judá primero».
es.B: Los israelitas se pusieron en marcha, subieron a Betel y consultaron a Dios: «¿Quién de nosotros debe subir primero a pelear contra los benjamitas?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «Judá irá primero».
es.R: Los israelitas subieron a Betel y le pidieron a Dios que los guiara. «¿Qué tribu debe ir primero a atacar a los hombres de Benjamín?», preguntaron. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «Judá irá primero».

fr.L: Et ils se levèrent et montèrent à Béthel, et ils consultèrent Dieu, et les fils d’Israël dirent : « Qui de nous montera le premier au combat contre les fils de Benjamin ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Juda, le premier. »
fr.B: Les Israélites se mirent en route et montèrent à Béthel, et ils consultèrent Dieu : « Lequel d’entre nous doit monter le premier combattre les Benjaminites ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit : « Juda montera le premier. »
fr.R: Les Israélites sont montés à Béthel et ils ont demandé à Dieu de les guider. « Quelle tribu doit aller la première attaquer les hommes de Benjamin ? » ont-ils demandé. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : « C’est Juda qui ira le premier. »

vi.L: Họ đứng dậy đi lên Bê-tên và cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời. Con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên nói: "Ai trong chúng con sẽ đi lên trước hết để giao chiến với con cháu Bên-gia-min?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Giu-đa trước hết."
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lên đường đi đến Bê-tên và cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời: "Ai trong chúng con nên đi lên trước để đánh người Bên-gia-min?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Giu-đa sẽ đi trước."
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi lên Bê-tên và cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời chỉ dẫn. Họ hỏi: "Chi tộc nào nên đi đánh người Bên-gia-min trước?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Giu-đa sẽ đi trước."

ko.L: 그들이 일어나 벧엘로 올라가서 하나님께 여쭈었다. 이스라엘 자손이 말했다. "우리 가운데 누가 먼저 올라가서 베냐민 자손과 싸워야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "유다가 먼저 가거라."
ko.B: 이스라엘 자손은 일어나 벧엘로 올라가서 하나님께 여쭈었다. "우리 가운데 어느 지파가 먼저 올라가서 베냐민 사람들과 싸워야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "유다가 먼저 가거라."
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 벧엘로 올라가서 하나님께 어떻게 해야 할지 여쭈었다. 그들이 물었다. "어느 지파가 먼저 가서 베냐민 사람들을 쳐야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "유다가 먼저 가거라."

pt.L: E se levantaram e subiram a Betel e consultaram a Deus, e os filhos de Israel disseram: "Quem de nós subirá primeiro à batalha contra os filhos de Benjamim?" E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Judá primeiro."
pt.B: Os israelitas partiram e subiram a Betel, e consultaram a Deus: "Quem de nós deve subir primeiro para lutar contra os benjamitas?" {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Judá deve ir primeiro."
pt.R: Os israelitas subiram a Betel e pediram a Deus que os orientasse. "Que tribo deve ir primeiro atacar os homens de Benjamim?", perguntaram. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Judá vai primeiro."

decisions.choice: asked God: sought God's answer through the priest
decisions.reason: To ask of God is to seek his decision, which in Israel was given through the priest (Numbers 27:21). Verses 27-28 say that the ark was at Bethel and Phinehas the priest served before it. The tribes ask in this way three times in this chapter (verses 18, 23, 27).

decisions.choice: Bethel: the town, not "the house of God"
decisions.reason: The name means "house of God" and is written as two words here. It is the town of that name, north of Gibeah, where the ark was at this time (verse 27). It is the place where God met Jacob (Genesis 28:19).

decisions.choice: who will go up first ... Judah first: the question that opens the book
decisions.reason: The tribes ask the same question in 1:1, and receive the same answer, "Judah" (1:2). There the enemy was the Canaanites; here it is Benjamin, one of Israel's own tribes. Unlike 1:2, God gives no promise of victory here.

decisions.choice: asked God (L, B); asked God for guidance (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used every time the tribes ask God or the LORD (verses 23, 27), as at 1:1. Readable says what the asking was for (m1).

decisions.choice: Which tribe; will go
decisions.reason: The answer names a tribe, so Readable says "tribe" in the question, as at 1:1.

decisions.choice: "wakamwomba Mungu awaongoze" (they asked God to guide them) at Readable, through these chapters
decisions.reason: Asking God here means seeking his answer through the priest (m1); Readable says what they were asking for, as the English Readable "asked God for guidance" does.

decisions.choice: Israel asks God in the formal polite style (합쇼체); the LORD answers in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for people speaking to God and God speaking to people.

decisions.choice: Israel asks God as "chúng con"; God answers with "phán"
decisions.reason: The prayer forms of the Genesis note; "phán" is kept for God speaking, as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: consultaram a Deus (L, B); pediram a Deus que os orientasse (R); Betel
decisions.reason: As 1:1 sets it for the whole book (also verses 23, 27): "consultar" is to seek God's decision (m1), and Readable says what the asking was for. "Betel" is the town (m2), as Genesis 28:19 has it in Portuguese. The question and answer keep the words of 1:1-2 where the Hebrew repeats them (m3).

source.text: וַיָּק֥וּמוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּֽחֲנ֖וּ עַל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And arose [the] sons of Israel in the morning and they camped against the Gibeah.

en.L: And the sons of Israel arose in the morning and camped against Gibeah.
en.B: The next morning the Israelites set out and camped facing Gibeah.
en.R: The next morning the Israelites marched out and set up camp near Gibeah.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakaondoka asubuhi, wakapiga kambi juu ya Gibea.
sw.B: Asubuhi iliyofuata Waisraeli waliondoka, wakapiga kambi wakiikabili Gibea.
sw.R: Asubuhi iliyofuata Waisraeli walitoka, wakapiga kambi karibu na Gibea.

es.L: Y se levantaron los hijos de Israel por la mañana y acamparon contra Guibeá.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente los israelitas se pusieron en marcha y acamparon frente a Guibeá.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente los israelitas salieron y acamparon cerca de Guibeá.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Israël se levèrent le matin et campèrent contre Guibea.
fr.B: Le lendemain matin, les Israélites se mirent en marche et établirent leur camp face à Guibea.
fr.R: Le lendemain matin, les Israélites se sont mis en marche, et ils ont installé leur camp près de Guibea.

vi.L: Sáng ra, con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đứng dậy và đóng trại đối diện Ghi-bê-a.
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên lên đường và đóng trại đối diện Ghi-bê-a.
vi.R: Sáng hôm sau, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kéo quân ra và đóng trại gần Ghi-bê-a.

ko.L: 이스라엘 자손이 아침에 일어나 기브아를 마주하여 진을 쳤다.
ko.B: 다음 날 아침 이스라엘 자손은 길을 떠나 기브아 맞은편에 진을 쳤다.
ko.R: 다음 날 아침 이스라엘 백성은 행군하여 기브아 근처에 진을 쳤다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel se levantaram de manhã e acamparam contra Gibeá.
pt.B: Na manhã seguinte, os israelitas partiram e acamparam diante de Gibeá.
pt.R: Na manhã seguinte, os israelitas marcharam e acamparam perto de Gibeá.

decisions.choice: camped against Gibeah: took up a position to attack the town
decisions.reason: To camp "against" a town is to set up camp facing it, ready to attack (Joshua 10:5).

decisions.choice: set out (B); marched out (R)
decisions.reason: "Arose" here means getting up and starting out, not only rising from sleep.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַיַּעַרְכ֨וּ אִתָּ֧ם אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִלְחָמָ֖ה אֶל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] men of Israel to the battle with Benjamin, and arranged with them [the] men of Israel battle at the Gibeah.

en.L: And the men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel arranged [the] battle [line] against them at Gibeah.
en.B: The men of Israel went out to fight Benjamin and drew up their battle lines against them at Gibeah.
en.R: The men of Israel went out to fight against Benjamin. They took their positions for battle at Gibeah.

sw.L: Nao watu wa Israeli wakatoka kwenda vitani kupigana na Benyamini, na watu wa Israeli wakapanga [safu za] vita juu yao huko Gibea.
sw.B: Watu wa Israeli walitoka kupigana na Benyamini, wakapanga safu zao za vita dhidi yao huko Gibea.
sw.R: Watu wa Israeli walitoka kupigana na Benyamini. Walichukua nafasi zao za vita huko Gibea.

es.L: Y salieron los hombres de Israel a la batalla contra Benjamín, y los hombres de Israel ordenaron [la] batalla contra ellos en Guibeá.
es.B: Los hombres de Israel salieron a pelear contra Benjamín y se pusieron en orden de batalla frente a ellos en Guibeá.
es.R: Los hombres de Israel salieron a pelear contra Benjamín. Tomaron sus posiciones para la batalla en Guibeá.

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Israël sortirent au combat contre Benjamin, et les hommes d’Israël rangèrent [la] bataille contre eux à Guibea.
fr.B: Les hommes d’Israël sortirent combattre Benjamin et se rangèrent en ordre de bataille contre eux à Guibea.
fr.R: Les hommes d’Israël sont sortis pour combattre Benjamin. Ils ont pris leurs positions de combat à Guibea.

vi.L: Những người Y-sơ-ra-ên ra giao chiến với Bên-gia-min, và những người Y-sơ-ra-ên dàn trận chống lại họ tại Ghi-bê-a.
vi.B: Những người Y-sơ-ra-ên ra đánh Bên-gia-min và dàn trận đối diện họ tại Ghi-bê-a.
vi.R: Những người Y-sơ-ra-ên ra đánh Bên-gia-min. Họ dàn quân sẵn sàng chiến đấu tại Ghi-bê-a.

ko.L: 이스라엘 사람들이 베냐민과 싸우러 나가서, 기브아에서 그들을 향하여 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 사람들은 베냐민과 싸우러 나가서, 기브아에서 그들을 향해 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 베냐민과 싸우러 나갔다. 그들은 기브아에서 싸울 자리를 잡았다.

pt.L: E os homens de Israel saíram à batalha contra Benjamim, e os homens de Israel dispuseram contra eles [a linha de] batalha em Gibeá.
pt.B: Os homens de Israel saíram para lutar contra Benjamim e formaram as suas linhas de batalha contra eles em Gibeá.
pt.R: Os homens de Israel saíram para lutar contra Benjamim. Eles tomaram posição para a batalha em Gibeá.

decisions.choice: arranged battle: drew up the army in its lines
decisions.reason: The verb means to set things in order. With "battle" it means placing the army in its ranks, ready to fight (1 Samuel 17:2, 8). The same phrase comes in verses 22, 30 and 33.

decisions.choice: arranged [the] battle [line] (L); drew up their battle lines (B); took their positions for battle (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used for this phrase at each level through the chapter (verses 22, 30, 33).

decisions.choice: "wakapanga [safu za] vita" (L), "wakapanga safu zao za vita" (B), "walichukua nafasi zao za vita" (R), through the chapter
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "arrange battle" means drawing up the battle lines (m1); the levels follow the English choices, and the same words are used each time the phrase returns.

decisions.choice: dispuseram [a linha de] batalha (L); formaram as suas linhas de batalha (B); tomaram posição para a batalha (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter (verses 22, 30, 33): the phrase for drawing up an army (m1) keeps one wording at each level, as the English does.

source.text: וַיֵּצְא֥וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִ֖ן מִן־הַגִּבְעָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁחִ֨יתוּ בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא שְׁנַ֨יִם וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] sons of Benjamin from the Gibeah, and they destroyed in Israel on the day the that two and twenty thousand man to [the] ground.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin came out from Gibeah, and they destroyed in Israel on that day 22,000 men to the ground.
en.B: Then the Benjaminites came out of Gibeah and cut down 22,000 men of Israel on the battlefield that day.
en.R: Then the men of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and attacked. That day they killed 22,000 Israelite soldiers.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakatoka Gibea, wakaangamiza katika Israeli siku hiyo watu 22,000 hata chini.
sw.B: Kisha Wabenyamini walitoka Gibea, wakawaua watu 22,000 wa Israeli uwanjani mwa vita siku hiyo.
sw.R: Kisha watu wa Benyamini walitoka Gibea, wakashambulia. Siku hiyo waliwaua askari 22,000 wa Israeli.

es.L: Y salieron los hijos de Benjamín de Guibeá, y destruyeron en Israel aquel día 22 000 hombres por tierra.
es.B: Entonces los benjamitas salieron de Guibeá y aquel día abatieron en el campo de batalla a 22 000 hombres de Israel.
es.R: Entonces los hombres de Benjamín salieron de Guibeá y atacaron. Aquel día mataron a 22 000 soldados israelitas.

fr.L: Et les fils de Benjamin sortirent de Guibea, et ils détruisirent en Israël, en ce jour-là, 22 000 hommes jusqu’à terre.
fr.B: Alors les Benjaminites sortirent de Guibea et abattirent ce jour-là sur le champ de bataille 22 000 hommes d’Israël.
fr.R: Alors les hommes de Benjamin sont sortis de Guibea et ils ont attaqué. Ce jour-là, ils ont tué 22 000 soldats israélites.

vi.L: Con cháu Bên-gia-min từ Ghi-bê-a kéo ra, và ngày ấy họ hủy diệt 22.000 người Y-sơ-ra-ên ngã xuống đất.
vi.B: Bấy giờ người Bên-gia-min từ Ghi-bê-a kéo ra và ngày ấy giết ngã 22.000 người Y-sơ-ra-ên trên chiến trường.
vi.R: Bấy giờ người Bên-gia-min từ Ghi-bê-a kéo ra tấn công. Ngày ấy họ giết 22.000 lính Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 베냐민 자손이 기브아에서 나와서, 그날 이스라엘 사람 이만 이천 명을 땅에 쳐 엎드러뜨렸다.
ko.B: 그러자 베냐민 사람들이 기브아에서 나와서, 그날 싸움터에서 이스라엘 사람 이만 이천 명을 쳐 죽였다.
ko.R: 그러자 베냐민 사람들이 기브아에서 나와 공격했다. 그날 그들은 이스라엘 군인 이만 이천 명을 죽였다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Benjamim saíram de Gibeá e abateram por terra em Israel, naquele dia, vinte e dois mil homens.
pt.B: Então os benjamitas saíram de Gibeá e, naquele dia, abateram vinte e dois mil homens de Israel no campo de batalha.
pt.R: Então os homens de Benjamim saíram de Gibeá e atacaram. Naquele dia, eles mataram vinte e dois mil soldados israelitas.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground: struck them down dead on the field
decisions.reason: The verb means to ruin or destroy. "To the ground" pictures the men falling where they fought. The phrase comes again in verse 25.

decisions.choice: 22,000: the tribes lose though God sent them
decisions.reason: The tribes asked God and went up as he said (verse 18), yet they are beaten. Though God told them who should go first, he did not promise them victory. The defeat sends them back to weep before the LORD (verse 23). On the size of the number see verse 2.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground (L); cut down ... on the battlefield (B); killed (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used again in verse 25.

decisions.choice: abateram por terra (L); abateram ... no campo de batalha (B); mataram (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to destroy, and "to the ground" pictures the men falling where they fought (m1). "Abater" is the Portuguese for striking men down, and Literal keeps "por terra"; the same wording returns in verse 25.

source.text: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֥ק הָעָ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ לַעֲרֹ֣ךְ מִלְחָמָ֔ה בַּמָּק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥רְכוּ שָׁ֖ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And strengthened itself the people, [the] men of Israel, and they again arranged battle in the place where they had arranged there on the day the first.

en.L: And the people, the men of Israel, strengthened themselves, and they again arranged [the] battle [line] in the place where they had arranged [it] on the first day.
en.B: But the army, the men of Israel, took courage and again drew up their battle lines in the same place where they had drawn them up on the first day.
en.R: But the Israelite army did not give up. They took courage and took their positions for battle again in the same place as on the first day.

sw.L: Nao watu, watu wa Israeli, wakajitia nguvu, wakapanga tena [safu za] vita mahali pale walipopanga [safu] siku ya kwanza.
sw.B: Lakini jeshi, watu wa Israeli, walijipa moyo, wakapanga tena safu zao za vita mahali pale pale walipozipanga siku ya kwanza.
sw.R: Lakini jeshi la Israeli halikukata tamaa. Walijipa moyo, wakachukua tena nafasi zao za vita mahali pale pale kama siku ya kwanza.

es.L: Y el pueblo, los hombres de Israel, se fortaleció, y volvieron a ordenar [la] batalla en el lugar donde la habían ordenado el primer día.
es.B: Pero el ejército, los hombres de Israel, cobró ánimo y volvió a ponerse en orden de batalla en el mismo lugar donde lo había hecho el primer día.
es.R: Pero el ejército israelita no se dio por vencido. Cobraron ánimo y volvieron a tomar sus posiciones para la batalla en el mismo lugar que el primer día.

fr.L: Et le peuple, les hommes d’Israël, se fortifia, et ils rangèrent de nouveau [la] bataille à l’endroit où ils [l’]avaient rangée le premier jour.
fr.B: Mais l’armée, les hommes d’Israël, reprit courage, et ils se rangèrent de nouveau en ordre de bataille au même endroit que le premier jour.
fr.R: Mais l’armée d’Israël n’a pas abandonné. Les soldats ont repris courage, et ils ont repris leurs positions de combat au même endroit que le premier jour.

vi.L: Dân chúng, là những người Y-sơ-ra-ên, tự làm cho mình mạnh mẽ, và lại dàn trận tại chỗ họ đã dàn trận ngày thứ nhất.
vi.B: Nhưng quân đội, là những người Y-sơ-ra-ên, lấy lại can đảm và lại dàn trận tại chính chỗ họ đã dàn trận ngày thứ nhất.
vi.R: Nhưng quân Y-sơ-ra-ên không bỏ cuộc. Họ lấy lại can đảm và lại dàn quân tại chính chỗ họ đã dàn quân ngày thứ nhất.

ko.L: 그러나 백성, 곧 이스라엘 사람들은 힘을 내어, 첫째 날에 전열을 갖추었던 그곳에 다시 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.B: 그러나 이스라엘 사람들의 군대는 용기를 내어, 첫째 날 전열을 갖추었던 바로 그 자리에 다시 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.R: 그러나 이스라엘 군대는 포기하지 않았다. 그들은 용기를 내어 첫째 날과 같은 자리에 다시 싸울 자리를 잡았다.

pt.L: E o povo, os homens de Israel, se fortaleceu, e voltaram a dispor [a linha de] batalha no lugar onde [a] tinham disposto no primeiro dia.
pt.B: Mas o exército, os homens de Israel, criou coragem e de novo formou as suas linhas de batalha no mesmo lugar onde as tinha formado no primeiro dia.
pt.R: Mas o exército israelita não desistiu. Os homens criaram coragem e tomaram posição para a batalha de novo, no mesmo lugar do primeiro dia.

decisions.choice: they again arranged battle: a summary told before the account of how it came about
decisions.reason: Verse 23, which comes next, tells of the weeping and the asking of the LORD that led to this second battle. Hebrew stories often give the outcome first and then go back to tell how it came about.

decisions.choice: strengthened itself: took courage, gathered its strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong. After losing 22,000 men, the army did not scatter but took heart to fight again.

decisions.choice: the people: the army
decisions.reason: "The people" in a story of war often means the fighting men, as here, where it is explained as "the men of Israel".

decisions.choice: arranged [the] battle [line] / drew up their battle lines / took their positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

source.text: וַיַּעֲל֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּבְכּ֣וּ לִפְנֵֽי־יְהוָה֮ עַד־הָעֶרֶב֒ וַיִּשְׁאֲל֤וּ בַֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאוֹסִ֗יף לָגֶ֨שֶׁת֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה עִם־בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן אָחִ֑י וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה עֲל֥וּ אֵלָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went up [the] sons of Israel and wept before Yahweh until the evening, and asked of Yahweh, saying, Shall I again draw near to the battle with [the] sons of Benjamin my brother? And said Yahweh, Go up against him.

en.L: And the sons of Israel went up and wept before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until the evening, and they asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I again draw near to battle against the sons of Benjamin my brother?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Go up against him."
en.B: The Israelites went up and wept before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until evening, and they asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should we again go into battle against our brothers the Benjaminites?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Go up against them."
en.R: The Israelites went up and cried before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until evening. They asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for guidance. "Should we fight against the men of Benjamin again? They are our relatives," they said. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Go and attack them."

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakapanda, wakalia mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mpaka jioni, wakamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakisema, "Je, nikaribie tena vitani kupigana na wana wa Benyamini ndugu yangu?" Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Pandeni juu yake."
sw.B: Waisraeli walipanda, wakalia mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mpaka jioni, wakamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Je, tuingie tena vitani kupigana na ndugu zetu Wabenyamini?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Pandeni mkawashambulie."
sw.R: Waisraeli walipanda, wakalia mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mpaka jioni. Walimwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awaongoze. Walisema, "Je, tupigane tena na watu wa Benyamini? Wao ni ndugu zetu." {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Nendeni mkawashambulie."

es.L: Y subieron los hijos de Israel y lloraron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} hasta la tarde, y consultaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «¿Volveré a acercarme a la batalla contra los hijos de Benjamín mi hermano?». Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «Sube contra él».
es.B: Los israelitas subieron y lloraron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} hasta la tarde, y consultaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Debemos volver a pelear contra nuestros hermanos los benjamitas?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «{{plural_you:Suban|Subid}} contra ellos».
es.R: Los israelitas subieron y lloraron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} hasta la tarde. Le pidieron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} que los guiara. «¿Debemos pelear otra vez contra los hombres de Benjamín? Son nuestros parientes», dijeron. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:atáquenlos|atacadlos}}».

fr.L: Et les fils d’Israël montèrent et pleurèrent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} jusqu’au soir, et ils consultèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} en disant : « M’approcherai-je encore pour combattre les fils de Benjamin, mon frère ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Montez contre lui. »
fr.B: Les Israélites montèrent pleurer devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} jusqu’au soir, et ils consultèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « Devons-nous encore engager le combat contre nos frères les Benjaminites ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit : « Montez contre eux. »
fr.R: Les Israélites sont montés pleurer devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} jusqu’au soir. Ils ont demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} de les guider : « Devons-nous encore combattre les hommes de Benjamin ? Ce sont nos frères », ont-ils dit. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : « Allez les attaquer. »

vi.L: Con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đi lên khóc lóc trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho đến chiều, và cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà nói: "Con có nên lại đến gần để giao chiến với con cháu Bên-gia-min, anh em của con không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Hãy đi lên đánh nó."
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi lên khóc lóc trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho đến chiều, và cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Chúng con có nên lại ra trận đánh anh em mình là người Bên-gia-min không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Hãy đi lên đánh chúng."
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi lên khóc trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho đến chiều. Họ cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chỉ dẫn. Họ hỏi: "Chúng con có nên đánh người Bên-gia-min nữa không? Họ là bà con của chúng con." {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Hãy đi đánh chúng."

ko.L: 이스라엘 자손이 올라가서 저녁까지 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 울며 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. "제가 다시 제 형제 베냐민 자손과 싸우러 나아가야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "그를 치러 올라가거라."
ko.B: 이스라엘 자손은 올라가서 저녁까지 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 울었다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. "우리가 우리 형제 베냐민 사람들과 다시 싸우러 나가야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "그들을 치러 올라가거라."
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 올라가서 저녁까지 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 울었다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 어떻게 해야 할지 여쭈었다. 그들이 말했다. "우리가 베냐민 사람들과 다시 싸워야 합니까? 그들은 우리 친척입니다." {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "가서 그들을 쳐라."

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel subiram e choraram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} até a tarde, e consultaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, dizendo: "Devo eu ainda me aproximar para a batalha contra os filhos de Benjamim, meu irmão?" E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Sobe contra ele."
pt.B: Os israelitas subiram e choraram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} até a tarde, e consultaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: "Devemos de novo entrar em batalha contra os nossos irmãos benjamitas?" {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Subam contra eles."
pt.R: Os israelitas subiram e choraram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} até a tarde. Eles pediram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} que os orientasse. "Devemos lutar de novo contra os homens de Benjamim? Eles são nossos parentes", disseram. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Vão e ataquem."

decisions.choice: they went up and wept: what happened before the battle of verse 22
decisions.reason: This verse goes back to tell what the tribes did between the two battles, as noted at verse 22. "Went up" is most likely to Bethel, where they asked God in verse 18 and go again in verse 26.

decisions.choice: shall I ... my brother: Israel speaks as one person of Benjamin as its brother
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "I" and "my", as if Israel were a single man asking whether to fight his brother. The question now is not who should lead but whether to fight at all.

decisions.choice: asked the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18: the tribes sought God's decision through the priest.

decisions.choice: go up against him: permission, but still no promise
decisions.reason: God tells them to go, but as in verse 18 he does not say they will win. Only at the third asking, after fasting and offerings, does he promise victory (verse 28).

decisions.choice: asked (L, B); asked ... for guidance (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: we ... our brothers ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, since the whole people is speaking of a whole tribe; Literal keeps the singular (m2).

decisions.choice: "¿Volveré ...?", "mi hermano", "Sube contra él" (L, singular); plural forms at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has Israel speak as one person of Benjamin as one brother, and the LORD answer in the singular (m2). Literal keeps the singular, with "tú" and no setting; Balanced and Readable use the plural, as the English does, so the LORD's answer to them takes the plural-you setting.

decisions.choice: "Con ... anh em của con" at Literal
decisions.reason: Israel speaks to God as one person and calls Benjamin its brother (meaning decision); Literal keeps the singular, the other levels say "chúng con", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Devo eu ... Sobe (L, singular, tu); Devemos ... Subam (B, R, plural, vocês)
decisions.reason: At Literal Israel speaks as one man (m2), and the LORD answers him in the singular with "tu", "Sobe", as God speaks to Israel in the singular (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md). Balanced and Readable use the plural, as the English does, and the LORD answers with "vocês". The same in verse 28.

source.text: וַיִּקְרְב֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And drew near [the] sons of Israel to [the] sons of Benjamin on the day the second.

en.L: And the sons of Israel drew near to the sons of Benjamin on the second day.
en.B: So the Israelites advanced against the Benjaminites on the second day.
en.R: So on the second day the Israelites went out against the men of Benjamin.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakawakaribia wana wa Benyamini siku ya pili.
sw.B: Basi Waisraeli waliwasogelea Wabenyamini kupigana nao siku ya pili.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo siku ya pili Waisraeli walitoka kupigana na watu wa Benyamini.

es.L: Y se acercaron los hijos de Israel a los hijos de Benjamín el segundo día.
es.B: Así que el segundo día los israelitas avanzaron contra los benjamitas.
es.R: Así que el segundo día los israelitas salieron contra los hombres de Benjamín.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Israël s’approchèrent des fils de Benjamin le deuxième jour.
fr.B: Le deuxième jour, les Israélites s’avancèrent donc contre les Benjaminites.
fr.R: Le deuxième jour, les Israélites sont donc sortis contre les hommes de Benjamin.

vi.L: Ngày thứ hai, con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gần con cháu Bên-gia-min.
vi.B: Vậy ngày thứ hai, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên tiến đánh người Bên-gia-min.
vi.R: Vậy ngày thứ hai, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra đánh người Bên-gia-min.

ko.L: 둘째 날에 이스라엘 자손이 베냐민 자손에게 가까이 나아갔다.
ko.B: 그래서 둘째 날에 이스라엘 자손은 베냐민 사람들을 향해 나아갔다.
ko.R: 그래서 둘째 날에 이스라엘 백성은 베냐민 사람들을 치러 나갔다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel se aproximaram dos filhos de Benjamim no segundo dia.
pt.B: Assim, no segundo dia, os israelitas avançaram contra os benjamitas.
pt.R: Então, no segundo dia, os israelitas saíram contra os homens de Benjamim.

decisions.choice: drew near: advanced to fight
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the question of verse 23, "Shall I again draw near to battle?" The tribes do what they asked about.

decisions.choice: advanced
decisions.reason: In a battle "drew near" means moved forward to attack, so Balanced says "advanced".

source.text: וַיֵּצֵא֩ בִנְיָמִ֨ן׀לִקְרָאתָ֥ם׀מִֽן־הַגִּבְעָה֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִי֒ וַיַּשְׁחִיתוּ֩ בִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל ע֗וֹד שְׁמֹנַ֨ת עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ אָ֑רְצָה כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה שֹׁ֥לְפֵי חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Benjamin to meet them from the Gibeah on the day the second, and they destroyed among [the] sons of Israel again eighteen thousand man to [the] ground; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.

en.L: And Benjamin went out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and they destroyed among the sons of Israel again 18,000 men to the ground; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.
en.B: Benjamin came out of Gibeah to meet them on the second day and again cut down 18,000 of the Israelites on the battlefield, all of them armed with swords.
en.R: On the second day Benjamin's army came out of Gibeah to meet them. Again they killed many Israelites: 18,000 soldiers, all armed with swords.

sw.L: Naye Benyamini akatoka Gibea kuwalaki siku ya pili, wakaangamiza tena katika wana wa Israeli watu 18,000 hata chini; hawa wote [walikuwa] wenye kufuta upanga.
sw.B: Siku ya pili Benyamini alitoka Gibea kuwalaki, akawaua tena Waisraeli 18,000 uwanjani mwa vita, wote wakiwa na panga.
sw.R: Siku ya pili jeshi la Benyamini lilitoka Gibea kuwalaki. Tena waliwaua Waisraeli wengi: askari 18,000, wote wenye panga.

es.L: Y salió Benjamín de Guibeá a su encuentro el segundo día, y destruyeron de nuevo entre los hijos de Israel 18 000 hombres por tierra; todos estos sacaban espada.
es.B: El segundo día Benjamín salió de Guibeá a su encuentro y abatió otra vez en el campo de batalla a 18 000 israelitas, todos ellos armados de espada.
es.R: El segundo día el ejército de Benjamín salió de Guibeá a su encuentro. Otra vez mataron a muchos israelitas: 18 000 soldados, todos armados con espadas.

fr.L: Et Benjamin sortit de Guibea à leur rencontre le deuxième jour, et ils détruisirent encore parmi les fils d’Israël 18 000 hommes jusqu’à terre ; tous ceux-là tiraient l’épée.
fr.B: Le deuxième jour, Benjamin sortit de Guibea à leur rencontre et abattit encore sur le champ de bataille 18 000 Israélites, tous armés de l’épée.
fr.R: Le deuxième jour, l’armée de Benjamin est sortie de Guibea pour les affronter. Ils ont encore tué beaucoup d’Israélites : 18 000 soldats, tous armés d’épées.

vi.L: Ngày thứ hai, Bên-gia-min từ Ghi-bê-a ra đón đánh họ, và lại hủy diệt 18.000 người trong con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên ngã xuống đất; tất cả đều là người cầm gươm.
vi.B: Ngày thứ hai, Bên-gia-min từ Ghi-bê-a ra đón đánh họ, và lại giết ngã 18.000 người Y-sơ-ra-ên trên chiến trường, tất cả đều là người cầm gươm.
vi.R: Ngày thứ hai, quân Bên-gia-min từ Ghi-bê-a kéo ra đón đánh họ. Họ lại giết nhiều người Y-sơ-ra-ên: 18.000 lính, tất cả đều cầm gươm.

ko.L: 둘째 날에 베냐민이 그들을 맞으러 기브아에서 나와서, 다시 이스라엘 자손 가운데 만 팔천 명을 땅에 쳐 엎드러뜨렸다. 이들은 모두 칼을 빼는 사람들이었다.
ko.B: 둘째 날에 베냐민이 그들을 맞으러 기브아에서 나와서, 다시 싸움터에서 이스라엘 자손 만 팔천 명을 쳐 죽였다. 그들은 모두 칼을 찬 군사들이었다.
ko.R: 둘째 날에 베냐민 군대가 그들을 맞으러 기브아에서 나왔다. 그들은 또 이스라엘 백성을 많이 죽였다. 죽은 사람은 만 팔천 명이었고, 모두 칼을 찬 군인들이었다.

pt.L: E Benjamim saiu de Gibeá ao encontro deles no segundo dia, e abateram por terra entre os filhos de Israel mais dezoito mil homens; todos estes puxavam [a] espada.
pt.B: No segundo dia, Benjamim saiu de Gibeá ao encontro deles e de novo abateu dezoito mil israelitas no campo de batalha, todos eles armados de espada.
pt.R: No segundo dia, o exército de Benjamim saiu de Gibeá para enfrentá-los. De novo mataram muitos israelitas: dezoito mil soldados, todos armados de espada.

decisions.choice: again 18,000: a second defeat after God said "go up"
decisions.reason: The tribes went up because the LORD told them to (verse 23), and they lose again. In two days they have lost 40,000 men. The story does not explain why; it shows the tribes driven to seek God more deeply in verse 26. On the size of the number see verse 2.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground (L); cut down ... on the battlefield (B); killed (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

records.literal_gloss: And went up all [the] sons of Israel and all the people and came [to] Bethel, and wept and sat there before Yahweh, and fasted on the day the that until the evening, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings before Yahweh.

en.L: And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel, and they wept and sat there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they fasted on that day until the evening, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel. They sat there weeping before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they fasted that day until evening and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel. They sat there and cried before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They went without food all that day until evening. They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

sw.L: Nao wana wote wa Israeli na watu wote wakapanda, wakafika Betheli, wakalia, wakaketi huko mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakafunga siku hiyo mpaka jioni, wakatoa sadaka za kuteketezwa na sadaka za amani mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Kisha Waisraeli wote, jeshi lote, walipanda Betheli. Waliketi huko wakilia mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakafunga siku hiyo mpaka jioni, wakatoa sadaka za kuteketezwa na sadaka za amani mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Kisha Waisraeli wote, jeshi lote, walipanda Betheli. Waliketi huko wakilia mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hawakula chakula siku nzima mpaka jioni. Walimtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} sadaka za kuteketezwa na sadaka za amani.

es.L: Y subieron todos los hijos de Israel y todo el pueblo, y llegaron a Betel, y lloraron y se sentaron allí delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y ayunaron aquel día hasta la tarde, y ofrecieron holocaustos y sacrificios de paz delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces todos los israelitas, el ejército entero, subieron a Betel. Se sentaron allí llorando delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, ayunaron aquel día hasta la tarde y ofrecieron holocaustos y sacrificios de paz delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces todos los israelitas, el ejército entero, subieron a Betel. Se sentaron allí y lloraron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Pasaron todo aquel día sin comer hasta la tarde. Ofrecieron holocaustos y sacrificios de paz {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et tous les fils d’Israël et tout le peuple montèrent et arrivèrent à Béthel, et ils pleurèrent et restèrent assis là devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ils jeûnèrent ce jour-là jusqu’au soir, et ils offrirent des holocaustes et des sacrifices de communion devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors tous les Israélites, toute l’armée, montèrent à Béthel. Ils restèrent assis là en pleurant devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; ils jeûnèrent ce jour-là jusqu’au soir et offrirent des holocaustes et des sacrifices de communion devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors tous les Israélites, toute l’armée, sont montés à Béthel. Ils sont restés assis là et ils ont pleuré devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils n’ont rien mangé de toute la journée, jusqu’au soir. Ils ont offert {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} des holocaustes et des sacrifices de communion.

vi.L: Toàn thể con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên và toàn dân đi lên đến Bê-tên, khóc lóc và ngồi ở đó trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, kiêng ăn ngày ấy cho đến chiều, và dâng tế lễ thiêu và tế lễ bình an trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Bấy giờ toàn thể dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, cả quân đội, đi lên Bê-tên. Họ ngồi khóc lóc ở đó trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, kiêng ăn ngày ấy cho đến chiều, và dâng tế lễ thiêu cùng tế lễ bình an trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Bấy giờ toàn thể dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, cả quân đội, đi lên Bê-tên. Họ ngồi ở đó và khóc trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ nhịn ăn suốt ngày ấy cho đến chiều. Họ dâng tế lễ thiêu và tế lễ bình an cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 그러자 이스라엘 자손 모두와 온 백성이 올라가 벧엘에 이르러, 거기에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 앉아 울었다. 그날 그들은 저녁까지 금식하고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 번제와 화목제를 드렸다.
ko.B: 그러자 이스라엘 자손, 곧 온 군대가 벧엘로 올라갔다. 그들은 거기에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 앉아 울었다. 그날 그들은 저녁까지 금식하고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 번제와 화목제를 드렸다.
ko.R: 그러자 이스라엘 백성, 곧 온 군대가 벧엘로 올라갔다. 그들은 거기에 앉아 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 울었다. 그날 그들은 저녁까지 아무것도 먹지 않았다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 번제와 화목제를 드렸다.

pt.L: E todos os filhos de Israel e todo o povo subiram e chegaram a Betel, e choraram e se sentaram ali diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e jejuaram naquele dia até a tarde, e ofereceram holocaustos e sacrifícios de comunhão diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Então todos os israelitas, o exército inteiro, subiram a Betel. Sentaram-se ali chorando diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, jejuaram naquele dia até a tarde e ofereceram holocaustos e sacrifícios de comunhão diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: Então todos os israelitas, o exército inteiro, subiram a Betel. Eles se sentaram ali e choraram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Ficaram sem comer o dia todo, até a tarde. Ofereceram holocaustos e sacrifícios de comunhão {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}.

decisions.choice: all the sons of Israel and all the people: the whole army together
decisions.reason: "The people" most likely means the fighting men, as in verse 22, so the two phrases say together that every one of them came. It could also mean that others besides the soldiers came with them.

decisions.choice: wept, sat, fasted: mourning and humbling themselves before God
decisions.reason: Sitting, weeping and fasting until evening were signs of grief and of seeking God with the whole heart (2 Samuel 12:16; Joel 2:12). Compared with verse 23, the tribes now add fasting and offerings: they come to God more humbly than before.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and peace offerings
decisions.reason: The burnt offering was wholly burned on the altar for God (Leviticus 1). The peace offering was shared, part burned and part eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 3). Together they sought God's favor and fellowship with him.

decisions.choice: the whole army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take "all the people" as explaining "all the Israelites" (m1). Literal keeps the two phrases side by side.

decisions.choice: went without food
decisions.reason: Readable says what fasting is.

decisions.choice: "tế lễ thiêu" and "tế lễ bình an"
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese names of the two offerings ("của lễ thiêu" in Genesis is the same word); "bình an" carries the sense of peace and fellowship in the Hebrew name.

decisions.choice: holocaustos e sacrifícios de comunhão
decisions.reason: The two offerings (m3) keep the terms of docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md, "o holocausto" and "o sacrifício de comunhão", at every level, as Leviticus 1 and 3 have them in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant of God: the sign of God's presence with Israel
decisions.reason: The ark was the chest that held the covenant tablets (Exodus 25:10-22; Deuteronomy 10:1-5). Where it was kept, there the priests sought God's answers for the people. This is the only time the book of Judges mentions it.

decisions.choice: there in those days: a note added to explain where and how they asked
decisions.reason: The narrator breaks off between "they asked" and the question (verse 28) to say that the ark was at Bethel at that time and who served before it. It explains why the tribes went to Bethel. Later the ark was kept at Shiloh (1 Samuel 4:3-4).

ko.L: 그 시대에 아론의 손자요 엘르아살의 아들인 비느하스가 그 앞에 서 있었다.) 그들이 말했다. "제가 다시 제 형제 베냐민 자손과 싸우러 나가야 합니까, 아니면 그만두어야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "올라가거라. 내일 내가 그를 네 손에 넘겨주겠다."

decisions.choice: Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron: the priest of the generation after Moses
decisions.reason: Phinehas is the grandson of Aaron who stood against Israel's sin at Peor (Numbers 25:7-13) and served in Joshua's time (Joshua 22:13). His name shows that these events took place early in the time of the judges, though the book tells them near its end.

decisions.choice: standing before it: serving as priest before the ark
decisions.reason: To "stand before" the LORD or his ark is to serve him as a priest (Deuteronomy 10:8; 18:7).

decisions.choice: tomorrow I will give him into your hand: now God promises victory
decisions.reason: For the first time in the chapter the LORD's answer includes a promise. The tribes asked twice before and lost; now, after fasting and offerings, they ask whether to stop, and God says he will give them the victory.

decisions.choice: or shall I cease: the tribes are ready to give up
decisions.reason: The question now has two sides. After two defeats the tribes ask whether they should stop fighting their brother altogether.

decisions.choice: we ... our brothers ... them ... you
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, Balanced and Readable use the plural for Israel and Benjamin. Readable also says "give you victory" for "give him into your hand" (1:2).

decisions.choice: the grandson of Aaron, was the priest who served there
decisions.reason: Readable says how Phinehas was related to Aaron and what his standing before the ark meant (m1, m2), and starts a new sentence for the question.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" and calls Israel "ngươi" (L, singular as the Hebrew) and "các ngươi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: God's words to Israel as a nation keep "ngươi" / "các ngươi" at every level (4:7); "Ta" takes the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence.

decisions.choice: Fineias, filho de Eleazar, filho de Arão
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the priest's name keeps the form of Exodus 6:25 in Portuguese, "Fineias", without the accent the 1990 spelling dropped, with "Eleazar" and "Arão" as in the Pentateuch (m1).

decisions.choice: ambushers: the plan that took Ai
decisions.reason: The tribes use the plan Joshua used against Ai: one force draws the defenders out of the city, while a hidden force waits to enter it behind them (Joshua 8:2-22). The rest of the chapter follows the same steps.

decisions.choice: around Gibeah: on more than one side of the town
decisions.reason: "Around" suggests men hidden at several points. Verse 33 tells of the main ambush coming from the west of Geba.

decisions.choice: hid soldiers ... ready to make a surprise attack
decisions.reason: Readable says what an ambush is.

decisions.choice: emboscadas (L); homens de emboscada (B)
decisions.reason: "Emboscada" is the word Joshua 8 uses in Portuguese for the hidden force at Ai, the plan the tribes now follow (m1); the same through verses 33-38.

en.L: And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day, and arranged [the] battle [line] against Gibeah as time by time.
en.B: On the third day the Israelites went up against the Benjaminites and drew up their battle lines against Gibeah as they had done before.
en.R: On the third day the Israelites went up to fight the men of Benjamin. They took their positions for battle at Gibeah just as they had done the other times.

es.R: Al tercer día los israelitas subieron a pelear contra los hombres de Benjamín. Tomaron sus posiciones para la batalla en Guibeá, igual que las otras veces.

fr.B: Le troisième jour, les Israélites montèrent contre les Benjaminites et se rangèrent en ordre de bataille contre Guibea, comme les autres fois.
fr.R: Le troisième jour, les Israélites sont montés combattre les hommes de Benjamin. Ils ont pris leurs positions de combat à Guibea, comme les autres fois.

vi.B: Ngày thứ ba, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi lên đánh người Bên-gia-min và dàn trận trước Ghi-bê-a như những lần trước.
vi.R: Ngày thứ ba, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi lên đánh người Bên-gia-min. Họ dàn quân tại Ghi-bê-a như những lần trước.

ko.L: 셋째 날에 이스라엘 자손이 베냐민 자손을 치러 올라가서, 전처럼 기브아를 향하여 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.B: 셋째 날에 이스라엘 자손은 베냐민 사람들을 치러 올라가서, 전처럼 기브아를 향해 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.R: 셋째 날에 이스라엘 백성은 베냐민 사람들과 싸우러 올라갔다. 그들은 전처럼 기브아에서 싸울 자리를 잡았다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel subiram contra os filhos de Benjamim no terceiro dia, e dispuseram [a linha de batalha] contra Gibeá como das outras vezes.
pt.B: No terceiro dia, os israelitas subiram contra os benjamitas e formaram as suas linhas de batalha contra Gibeá, como tinham feito antes.
pt.R: No terceiro dia, os israelitas subiram para lutar contra os homens de Benjamim. Eles tomaram posição para a batalha em Gibeá, como tinham feito das outras vezes.

decisions.choice: as time by time: as on the other occasions
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as before", the same way they had done twice already. It is part of the plan: Benjamin is to think this is one more battle like the others (verse 32).

decisions.choice: arranged
decisions.reason: As in verse 20: drew up the army for battle; here the word "battle" is understood.

decisions.choice: arranged [the] battle [line] / drew up their battle lines / took their positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. Literal brackets "the battle line", which the Hebrew leaves understood here.

source.text: וַיֵּצְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִן֙ לִקְרַ֣את הָעָ֔ם הָנְתְּק֖וּ מִן־הָעִ֑יר וַיָּחֵ֡לּוּ לְהַכּוֹת֩ מֵהָעָ֨ם חֲלָלִ֜ים כְּפַ֣עַם׀בְּפַ֗עַם בַּֽמְסִלּוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַחַ֜ת עֹלָ֣ה בֵֽית־אֵ֗ל וְאַחַ֤ת גִּבְעָ֨תָה֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה כִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] sons of Benjamin to meet the people; they were drawn away from the city. And they began to strike from the people slain, as time by time, on the highways, of which one goes up [to] Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field, about thirty man in Israel.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people; they were drawn away from the city. And they began to strike [some] of the people, slain as time by time, on the highways, one of which goes up to Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men in Israel.
en.B: The Benjaminites came out to meet the army and were drawn away from the town. As before, they began to strike down some of the troops on the roads, one leading up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, in the open country. They killed about thirty men of Israel.
en.R: The men of Benjamin came out to fight the army, and the Israelites led them away from the town. As before, the men of Benjamin began killing some of the soldiers in the open country along the roads. One road went to Bethel and the other to Gibeah. They killed about thirty men of Israel.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakatoka kuwalaki watu; wakavutwa mbali na mji. Wakaanza kuwapiga [baadhi] ya watu, waliouawa kama mara zile nyingine, katika njia kuu, moja yao ipandayo Betheli na moja Gibea mashambani, watu wapata thelathini katika Israeli.
sw.B: Wabenyamini walitoka kulilaki jeshi, wakavutwa mbali na mji. Kama mara zile nyingine, walianza kuwaua baadhi ya askari katika njia kuu, moja ikipanda Betheli na nyingine Gibea, huko mashambani. Waliwaua watu wapata thelathini wa Israeli.
sw.R: Watu wa Benyamini walitoka kupigana na jeshi, na Waisraeli wakawavuta mbali na mji. Kama mara zile nyingine, watu wa Benyamini walianza kuwaua baadhi ya askari mashambani kando ya njia. Njia moja ilikwenda Betheli na nyingine Gibea. Waliwaua watu wapata thelathini wa Israeli.

es.L: Y salieron los hijos de Benjamín al encuentro del pueblo; fueron alejados de la ciudad. Y comenzaron a herir [a algunos] del pueblo, muertos como las otras veces, en los caminos, uno de los cuales sube a Betel y otro a Guibeá en el campo, unos treinta hombres de Israel.
es.B: Los benjamitas salieron al encuentro del ejército y se dejaron alejar de la ciudad. Como antes, comenzaron a abatir a algunos de la tropa en los caminos, uno que sube a Betel y otro a Guibeá, en campo abierto. Mataron a unos treinta hombres de Israel.
es.R: Los hombres de Benjamín salieron a pelear contra el ejército, y los israelitas los alejaron del pueblo. Como antes, los de Benjamín comenzaron a matar a algunos soldados en campo abierto, a lo largo de los caminos. Un camino iba a Betel y el otro a Guibeá. Mataron a unos treinta hombres de Israel.

fr.L: Et les fils de Benjamin sortirent à la rencontre du peuple ; ils furent attirés loin de la ville. Et ils commencèrent à frapper [quelques-uns] du peuple, des morts, comme chaque fois, sur les routes, dont l’une monte à Béthel et l’autre à Guibea, dans la campagne : environ trente hommes d’Israël.
fr.B: Les Benjaminites sortirent à la rencontre de l’armée et se laissèrent attirer loin de la ville. Comme les autres fois, ils commencèrent à abattre quelques hommes de la troupe sur les routes, dont l’une monte à Béthel et l’autre à Guibea, en rase campagne. Ils tuèrent environ trente hommes d’Israël.
fr.R: Les hommes de Benjamin sont sortis pour combattre l’armée, et les Israélites les ont attirés loin de la ville. Comme les autres fois, les hommes de Benjamin ont commencé à tuer quelques soldats dans la campagne, le long des routes. Une route allait à Béthel et l’autre à Guibea. Ils ont tué environ trente hommes d’Israël.

vi.L: Con cháu Bên-gia-min kéo ra đón đánh dân chúng; họ bị dụ xa khỏi thành. Họ bắt đầu đánh giết [một số] người trong dân chúng như những lần trước, trên các đường cái, một đường đi lên Bê-tên và một đường đến Ghi-bê-a ngoài đồng, khoảng ba mươi người Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Người Bên-gia-min kéo ra đón đánh quân đội và bị dụ xa khỏi thành. Như lần trước, họ bắt đầu giết một số quân lính trên các đường cái ngoài đồng, một đường đi lên Bê-tên và một đường đến Ghi-bê-a. Họ giết khoảng ba mươi người Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Người Bên-gia-min kéo ra đánh quân đội, và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên dụ họ đi xa khỏi thành. Như lần trước, người Bên-gia-min bắt đầu giết một số lính ngoài đồng, dọc theo các con đường. Một đường đi Bê-tên, còn đường kia đi Ghi-bê-a. Họ giết khoảng ba mươi người Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 베냐민 자손이 백성을 맞으러 나왔다가 성읍에서 멀리 끌려 나왔다. 그들은 전처럼 큰길에서, 곧 하나는 벧엘로 올라가고 하나는 들판의 기브아로 가는 길에서 백성 가운데 몇을 쳐 죽이기 시작하였는데, 이스라엘 사람 서른 명쯤이었다.
ko.B: 베냐민 사람들은 이스라엘 군대를 맞으러 나왔다가 성읍에서 멀리 끌려 나왔다. 그들은 전처럼 들판의 길, 곧 벧엘로 올라가는 길과 기브아로 가는 길에서 이스라엘 군사 몇을 쳐 죽이기 시작했다. 그들은 이스라엘 사람 서른 명쯤을 죽였다.
ko.R: 베냐민 사람들이 이스라엘 군대와 싸우러 나왔고, 이스라엘 백성은 그들을 성에서 멀리 끌어냈다. 베냐민 사람들은 전처럼 들판의 길에서 이스라엘 군인들을 죽이기 시작했다. 한 길은 벧엘로, 다른 길은 기브아로 가는 길이었다. 그들은 이스라엘 사람 서른 명쯤을 죽였다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Benjamim saíram ao encontro do povo; foram atraídos para longe da cidade. E começaram a ferir [alguns] do povo, mortos como das outras vezes, nas estradas, das quais uma sobe a Betel e outra a Gibeá, no campo, cerca de trinta homens de Israel.
pt.B: Os benjamitas saíram ao encontro do exército e foram atraídos para longe da cidade. Como antes, começaram a abater alguns dos soldados nas estradas, uma que sobe a Betel e a outra a Gibeá, em campo aberto. Mataram cerca de trinta homens de Israel.
pt.R: Os homens de Benjamim saíram para lutar contra o exército, e os israelitas os atraíram para longe da cidade. Como antes, os homens de Benjamim começaram a matar alguns soldados em campo aberto, ao longo das estradas. Uma estrada ia para Betel, e a outra para Gibeá. Eles mataram cerca de trinta homens de Israel.

decisions.choice: they were drawn away from the city: pulled away by the tribes' pretended retreat
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: the Benjaminites were led away from Gibeah without knowing it. Verse 32 tells how the tribes planned it, and Joshua 8:16 uses the same verb of the men of Ai.

decisions.choice: Gibeah in the field: as the Hebrew has it, though Gibeah is the city they left
decisions.reason: The Benjaminites have just left Gibeah, so a road "to Gibeah" is surprising. It may mean a road back toward Gibeah across open country. It may also be a slip for Gibeon, a town to the west whose name is very like it in Hebrew; the Hebrew text has Gibeah.

decisions.choice: highways: the main roads
decisions.reason: The word means a built-up road or highway. Fighting on the roads in open country, away from the town, was what the tribes wanted (verse 32).

decisions.choice: They killed about thirty men of Israel.
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the number in its own sentence; in the Hebrew it comes at the end of the long description of the roads.

decisions.choice: the Israelites led them
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive verb active and says who drew them away (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן נִגָּפִ֥ים הֵ֛ם לְפָנֵ֖ינוּ כְּבָרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָמְר֗וּ נָנ֨וּסָה֙ וּֽנְתַקְּנֻ֔הוּ מִן־הָעִ֖יר אֶל־הַֽמְסִלּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] sons of Benjamin, They are struck down before us as at the first. And [the] sons of Israel said, Let us flee and draw him away from the city to the highways.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin said, "They are struck down before us as at the first." But the sons of Israel said, "Let us flee and draw him away from the city to the highways."
en.B: The Benjaminites said, "They are being beaten by us as they were before." But the Israelites had said, "Let us run away and draw them out from the town onto the roads."
en.R: The men of Benjamin said, "We are beating them, just as we did before." But the Israelites had planned this. They had said, "Let us run away, so that we can lead them away from the town and onto the roads."

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakasema, "Wamepigwa mbele yetu kama mara ya kwanza." Lakini wana wa Israeli wakasema, "Na tukimbie, tumvute mbali na mji mpaka kwenye njia kuu."
sw.B: Wabenyamini walisema, "Wanashindwa mbele yetu kama walivyoshindwa mwanzoni." Lakini Waisraeli walikuwa wamesema, "Tukimbie, tuwavute kutoka mjini mpaka kwenye njia kuu."
sw.R: Watu wa Benyamini walisema, "Tunawashinda, kama tulivyofanya mwanzoni." Lakini Waisraeli walikuwa wamepanga jambo hili. Walikuwa wamesema, "Tukimbie, ili tuwavute mbali na mji mpaka kwenye njia."

es.L: Y dijeron los hijos de Benjamín: «Son derrotados delante de nosotros como al principio». Pero los hijos de Israel dijeron: «Huyamos y alejémoslo de la ciudad hacia los caminos».
es.B: Los benjamitas decían: «Los estamos derrotando como la primera vez». Pero los israelitas habían dicho: «Huyamos y saquémoslos de la ciudad hacia los caminos».
es.R: Los hombres de Benjamín decían: «Les estamos ganando, igual que antes». Pero los israelitas lo habían planeado así. Habían dicho: «Huyamos, para alejarlos del pueblo y llevarlos a los caminos».

fr.L: Et les fils de Benjamin dirent : « Ils sont battus devant nous comme au début. » Mais les fils d’Israël dirent : « Fuyons, et attirons-le loin de la ville vers les routes. »
fr.B: Les Benjaminites se dirent : « Ils sont battus devant nous comme la première fois. » Mais les Israélites avaient dit : « Fuyons, pour les attirer loin de la ville, sur les routes. »
fr.R: Les hommes de Benjamin ont dit : « Nous les battons, comme la première fois. » Mais les Israélites avaient prévu cela. Ils avaient dit : « Fuyons, pour les attirer loin de la ville, sur les routes. »

vi.L: Con cháu Bên-gia-min nói: "Chúng bị đánh bại trước mặt chúng ta như lần trước." Nhưng con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên đã nói: "Chúng ta hãy chạy trốn, và dụ nó ra xa khỏi thành đến các đường cái."
vi.B: Người Bên-gia-min nói: "Chúng lại thua chúng ta như lần trước." Nhưng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã bàn với nhau: "Chúng ta hãy bỏ chạy, dụ chúng ra xa khỏi thành đến các đường cái."
vi.R: Người Bên-gia-min nói: "Chúng ta đang thắng chúng, như lần trước." Nhưng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã tính trước việc này. Họ đã nói: "Chúng ta hãy bỏ chạy, để dụ chúng ra xa khỏi thành và đến các con đường."

ko.L: 베냐민 자손이 말했다. "그들이 처음처럼 우리 앞에서 쓰러진다." 그러나 이스라엘 자손은 "우리가 도망하여 그를 성읍에서 큰길로 끌어내자" 하고 말했었다.
ko.B: 베냐민 사람들은 "그들이 처음처럼 우리에게 지고 있다" 하고 말했다. 그러나 이스라엘 자손은 이미 "우리가 도망쳐서 그들을 성읍에서 큰길로 끌어내자" 하고 말해 두었던 것이다.
ko.R: 베냐민 사람들은 "우리가 전처럼 그들을 이기고 있다" 하고 말했다. 그러나 그것은 이스라엘 백성이 미리 계획한 일이었다. 그들은 "도망치는 척해서, 그들을 성에서 끌어내어 큰길로 나오게 하자" 하고 말해 두었다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Benjamim disseram: "Eles estão sendo derrotados diante de nós como no princípio." Mas os filhos de Israel disseram: "Fujamos e atraiamo-lo para longe da cidade, para as estradas."
pt.B: Os benjamitas diziam: "Eles estão sendo derrotados por nós, como da outra vez." Mas os israelitas tinham dito: "Vamos fugir e atraí-los para longe da cidade, para as estradas."
pt.R: Os homens de Benjamim disseram: "Estamos vencendo os israelitas, como da outra vez." Mas os israelitas tinham planejado isso. Eles tinham dito: "Vamos fugir, para atrair os homens de Benjamim para longe da cidade e para as estradas."

decisions.choice: and the sons of Israel said: the plan made before the battle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two sayings side by side. The tribes' words are the plan they had made beforehand, now told to show why Benjamin was wrong.

decisions.choice: struck down: defeated
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an army beaten in battle (verse 36; 1 Samuel 4:2).

decisions.choice: had said (B); had planned this. They had said (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the tribes' words came before, as the plan (m1).

source.text: וְכֹ֣ל׀אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל קָ֚מוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ וַיַּעַרְכ֖וּ בְּבַ֣עַל תָּמָ֑ר וְאֹרֵ֧ב יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵגִ֥יחַ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ מִמַּֽעֲרֵה־גָֽבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And every man of Israel rose from his place and arranged at Baal-tamar, and [the] ambush of Israel [was] bursting out from its place, from [the] open place of Geba.

en.L: And all the men of Israel rose from their place and arranged [the battle line] at Baal-tamar, and the ambush of Israel was bursting out from its place, from the open place of Geba.
en.B: All the men of Israel rose up from where they were and drew up their battle lines at Baal-tamar, while the men of Israel in ambush burst out from their position west of Geba.
en.R: The main Israelite army left its position and took its positions for battle at Baal-tamar. At the same time the soldiers who were hiding west of Geba rushed out from their hiding place.

sw.L: Nao watu wote wa Israeli wakainuka kutoka mahali pao, wakapanga [safu za vita] huko Baal-tamari, nao waviziaji wa Israeli walikuwa wakitoka kwa kasi mahali pao, kutoka uwanda wa Geba.
sw.B: Watu wote wa Israeli waliinuka kutoka mahali walipokuwa, wakapanga safu zao za vita huko Baal-tamari, wakati watu wa Israeli waliokuwa wakivizia walitoka kwa kasi mahali pao upande wa magharibi wa Geba.
sw.R: Jeshi kuu la Israeli liliacha mahali pake, likachukua nafasi zake za vita huko Baal-tamari. Wakati huo huo askari waliokuwa wamejificha magharibi ya Geba walitoka kwa kasi katika maficho yao.

es.L: Y todos los hombres de Israel se levantaron de su lugar y se ordenaron [en batalla] en Baal-tamar, y la emboscada de Israel irrumpía de su lugar, del claro de Geba.
es.B: Todos los hombres de Israel se levantaron de donde estaban y se pusieron en orden de batalla en Baal-tamar, mientras los israelitas emboscados irrumpían desde su posición al oeste de Geba.
es.R: El grueso del ejército israelita dejó su lugar y tomó sus posiciones para la batalla en Baal-tamar. Al mismo tiempo, los soldados que estaban escondidos al oeste de Geba salieron corriendo de su escondite.

fr.L: Et tous les hommes d’Israël se levèrent de leur place et se rangèrent à Baal-Tamar, et l’embuscade d’Israël surgissait de sa place, de la clairière de Guéba.
fr.B: Tous les hommes d’Israël quittèrent leur position et se rangèrent en ordre de bataille à Baal-Tamar, pendant que les Israélites postés en embuscade surgissaient de leur cachette, à l’ouest de Guéba.
fr.R: Le gros de l’armée israélite a quitté sa position et a pris ses positions de combat à Baal-Tamar. Au même moment, les soldats qui étaient cachés à l’ouest de Guéba sont sortis de leur cachette en courant.

vi.L: Tất cả những người Y-sơ-ra-ên đứng dậy từ chỗ mình và dàn [trận] tại Ba-anh-Tha-ma, còn quân phục kích của Y-sơ-ra-ên xông ra khỏi chỗ mình, từ khoảng trống của Ghê-ba.
vi.B: Tất cả những người Y-sơ-ra-ên rời chỗ mình và dàn trận tại Ba-anh-Tha-ma, trong khi quân phục kích của Y-sơ-ra-ên xông ra khỏi chỗ nấp ở phía tây Ghê-ba.
vi.R: Đại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên rời chỗ mình và dàn quân tại Ba-anh-Tha-ma. Cùng lúc ấy, quân đang ẩn nấp ở phía tây Ghê-ba xông ra khỏi chỗ nấp.

ko.L: 이스라엘의 모든 사람이 자기 자리에서 일어나 바알다말에서 [전열을] 갖추었고, 이스라엘의 복병은 자기 자리, 곧 게바의 빈터에서 뛰쳐나왔다.
ko.B: 이스라엘의 모든 사람이 자기 자리에서 일어나 바알다말에서 전열을 갖추었고, 그동안 숨어 있던 이스라엘 군사들은 게바 서쪽의 자기 자리에서 뛰쳐나왔다.
ko.R: 이스라엘의 본대는 자기 자리를 떠나 바알다말에서 싸울 자리를 잡았다. 그와 동시에 게바 서쪽에 숨어 있던 군인들이 숨은 곳에서 뛰쳐나왔다.

pt.L: E todos os homens de Israel se levantaram do seu lugar e dispuseram [a linha de batalha] em Baal-Tamar, e a emboscada de Israel irrompia do seu lugar, do descampado de Geba.
pt.B: Todos os homens de Israel se levantaram de onde estavam e formaram as suas linhas de batalha em Baal-Tamar, enquanto os homens de Israel que estavam de emboscada irrompiam da sua posição, a oeste de Geba.
pt.R: O exército principal de Israel saiu da sua posição e tomou posição para a batalha em Baal-Tamar. Ao mesmo tempo, os soldados que estavam escondidos a oeste de Geba saíram correndo do seu esconderijo.

decisions.choice: Baal-tamar: a place near Gibeah, not known today
decisions.reason: The name means "lord of the palm tree". Its site is not known, but it lay near Gibeah, where the main army turned to fight.

decisions.choice: the open place of Geba: a clearing near Geba, or west of Geba
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is rare and may mean a bare or open place. The Greek translation and the Latin read it as "west of" and some read "Gibeah" for "Geba". The ambush came out from an open area beside one of these two towns.

decisions.choice: was bursting out: at the same moment
decisions.reason: The verb form describes action going on at the same time as the main army's turn. As the army turned to face Benjamin, the ambush rushed out behind them.

decisions.choice: west of Geba
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the reading "west of" as the most likely sense of the rare word (m2); Literal keeps "the open place". Readable also says "west".

decisions.choice: arranged [the battle line] / drew up their battle lines / took its positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

decisions.choice: Baal-Tamar; o descampado de Geba (L); a oeste de Geba (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Baal-Tamar" writes the name as Numbers writes Baal-Peor in Portuguese (m1). Literal says "descampado", an open stretch of land, for the rare word (m2); Balanced and Readable follow the reading "west of", as the English does.

source.text: וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ מִנֶּ֨גֶד לַגִּבְעָ֜ה עֲשֶׂרֶת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אִ֤ישׁ בָּחוּר֙ מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה כָּבֵ֑דָה וְהֵם֙ לֹ֣א יָדְע֔וּ כִּֽי־נֹגַ֥עַת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הָרָעָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came from before the Gibeah ten thousand man chosen from all Israel, and the battle [was] heavy; and they did not know that touching upon them [was] the disaster.

en.L: And there came from opposite Gibeah 10,000 chosen men from all Israel, and the battle was heavy; and they did not know that the disaster was touching them.
en.B: Then 10,000 chosen men from all Israel came against Gibeah, and the fighting was fierce. The Benjaminites did not realize that disaster was about to strike them.
en.R: Then 10,000 of Israel's best soldiers attacked Gibeah. The fighting was hard. The men of Benjamin did not know that disaster was about to fall on them.

sw.L: Wakaja kutoka mkabala na Gibea watu 10,000 waliochaguliwa kutoka Israeli wote, na vita vikawa vikali; wala hawakujua ya kuwa maafa yalikuwa yakiwagusa.
sw.B: Kisha watu 10,000 waliochaguliwa kutoka Israeli wote waliishambulia Gibea, na mapigano yakawa makali. Wabenyamini hawakutambua kwamba maafa yalikuwa karibu kuwapata.
sw.R: Kisha askari 10,000 bora wa Israeli waliishambulia Gibea. Mapigano yalikuwa makali. Watu wa Benyamini hawakujua kwamba maafa yalikuwa karibu kuwaangukia.

es.L: Y vinieron frente a Guibeá 10 000 hombres escogidos de todo Israel, y la batalla fue dura; y ellos no sabían que la desgracia los alcanzaba.
es.B: Entonces 10 000 hombres escogidos de todo Israel atacaron Guibeá, y la lucha fue encarnizada. Los benjamitas no se dieron cuenta de que la desgracia estaba a punto de caer sobre ellos.
es.R: Entonces 10 000 de los mejores soldados de Israel atacaron Guibeá. La lucha fue dura. Los hombres de Benjamín no sabían que la desgracia estaba a punto de caer sobre ellos.

fr.L: Et il vint d’en face de Guibea 10 000 hommes d’élite de tout Israël, et le combat fut rude ; et ils ne savaient pas que le malheur les atteignait.
fr.B: Puis 10 000 hommes d’élite de tout Israël arrivèrent face à Guibea, et le combat fut acharné. Les Benjaminites ne se doutaient pas que le malheur allait les frapper.
fr.R: Ensuite, 10 000 des meilleurs soldats d’Israël ont attaqué Guibea. Le combat a été dur. Les hommes de Benjamin ne savaient pas que le malheur allait tomber sur eux.

vi.L: Mười nghìn người tinh nhuệ từ khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên kéo đến trước Ghi-bê-a, và trận chiến thật ác liệt; nhưng họ không biết rằng tai họa đã chạm đến mình.
vi.B: Bấy giờ 10.000 người tinh nhuệ từ khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên kéo đến đánh Ghi-bê-a, và trận chiến rất ác liệt. Người Bên-gia-min không nhận ra tai họa sắp giáng xuống mình.
vi.R: Bấy giờ 10.000 lính giỏi nhất của Y-sơ-ra-ên tấn công Ghi-bê-a. Trận đánh rất gay go. Người Bên-gia-min không biết tai họa sắp đổ xuống trên mình.

ko.L: 온 이스라엘에서 뽑힌 사람 만 명이 기브아 맞은편에서 왔고, 싸움이 치열하였다. 그러나 그들은 재앙이 자기들에게 닥쳐온 줄을 알지 못하였다.
ko.B: 그때 온 이스라엘에서 뽑힌 정예 군사 만 명이 기브아로 쳐들어갔고, 싸움은 치열했다. 베냐민 사람들은 재앙이 자기들에게 닥치려는 줄을 알지 못했다.
ko.R: 그때 이스라엘의 가장 뛰어난 군인 만 명이 기브아를 공격했다. 싸움은 아주 힘들었다. 베냐민 사람들은 재앙이 곧 자기들에게 닥치리라는 것을 알지 못했다.

pt.L: E vieram defronte de Gibeá dez mil homens escolhidos de todo o Israel, e a batalha foi pesada; e eles não sabiam que a desgraça os estava alcançando.
pt.B: Então dez mil homens escolhidos de todo o Israel atacaram Gibeá, e a luta foi violenta. Os benjamitas não perceberam que a desgraça estava para cair sobre eles.
pt.R: Então dez mil dos melhores soldados de Israel atacaram Gibeá. A luta foi dura. Os homens de Benjamim não sabiam que a desgraça estava para cair sobre eles.

decisions.choice: came from before Gibeah: came at Gibeah from the front, or from opposite it
decisions.reason: The words "from before" may mean the ambush came from the side facing Gibeah, or that the 10,000 attacked the town head on. Either way it is the force that would take Gibeah.

decisions.choice: they did not know: the Benjaminites
decisions.reason: "They" are the men of Benjamin, still fighting on the roads, who did not see the ambush taking their town behind them (verses 40-41).

decisions.choice: the disaster touching them: ruin about to reach them
decisions.reason: The word is the same one used for the "evil" of Gibeah in verses 3, 12 and 13. The evil that Benjamin refused to remove now comes upon them as disaster.

decisions.choice: The Benjaminites / The men of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are (m2).

decisions.choice: a desgraça
decisions.reason: The word is the "mal" of Gibeah in verses 3, 12-13 (m3); Portuguese cannot keep one word for both, so it says "desgraça", which names a ruin that falls on someone and can be heard as its fruit; the same in verse 41.

source.text: וַיִּגֹּ֨ף יְהוָ֥ה׀אֶֽת־בִּנְיָמִן֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּשְׁחִיתוּ֩ בְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בְּבִנְיָמִן֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה אֶ֛לֶף וּמֵאָ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה שֹׁ֥לֵף חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck Yahweh Benjamin before Israel, and destroyed [the] sons of Israel in Benjamin on the day the that twenty and five thousand and a hundred man; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed in Benjamin on that day 25,100 men; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} defeated Benjamin before Israel, and that day the Israelites cut down 25,100 men of Benjamin, all of them armed with swords.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel victory over Benjamin. That day the Israelites killed 25,100 of Benjamin's soldiers, all armed with swords.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akampiga Benyamini mbele ya Israeli, na wana wa Israeli wakaangamiza katika Benyamini siku hiyo watu 25,100; hawa wote [walikuwa] wenye kufuta upanga.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimshinda Benyamini mbele ya Israeli, na siku hiyo Waisraeli waliwaua watu 25,100 wa Benyamini, wote wakiwa na panga.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa Israeli ushindi juu ya Benyamini. Siku hiyo Waisraeli waliwaua askari 25,100 wa Benyamini, wote wenye panga.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hirió a Benjamín delante de Israel, y los hijos de Israel destruyeron en Benjamín aquel día 25 100 hombres; todos estos sacaban espada.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} derrotó a Benjamín delante de Israel, y aquel día los israelitas abatieron a 25 100 hombres de Benjamín, todos ellos armados de espada.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Israel la victoria sobre Benjamín. Aquel día los israelitas mataron a 25 100 soldados de Benjamín, todos armados con espadas.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} frappa Benjamin devant Israël, et les fils d’Israël détruisirent en Benjamin, en ce jour-là, 25 100 hommes ; tous ceux-là tiraient l’épée.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} battit Benjamin devant Israël, et ce jour-là les Israélites abattirent 25 100 hommes de Benjamin, tous armés de l’épée.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné à Israël la victoire sur Benjamin. Ce jour-là, les Israélites ont tué 25 100 soldats de Benjamin, tous armés d’épées.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đánh Bên-gia-min trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, và ngày ấy con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên hủy diệt 25.100 người của Bên-gia-min; tất cả đều là người cầm gươm.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đánh bại Bên-gia-min trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, và ngày ấy dân Y-sơ-ra-ên giết ngã 25.100 người Bên-gia-min, tất cả đều là người cầm gươm.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho Y-sơ-ra-ên chiến thắng Bên-gia-min. Ngày ấy dân Y-sơ-ra-ên giết 25.100 lính Bên-gia-min, tất cả đều cầm gươm.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 앞에서 베냐민을 치셨다. 그날 이스라엘 자손은 베냐민 가운데 이만 오천백 명을 쳐 죽였다. 이들은 모두 칼을 빼는 사람들이었다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 베냐민을 이스라엘 앞에서 쳐부수셨다. 그날 이스라엘 자손은 베냐민 사람 이만 오천백 명을 쳐 죽였다. 그들은 모두 칼을 찬 군사들이었다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘이 베냐민을 이기게 해 주셨다. 그날 이스라엘 백성은 베냐민 군인 이만 오천백 명을 죽였다. 그들은 모두 칼을 찬 군인들이었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} feriu Benjamim diante de Israel, e os filhos de Israel abateram em Benjamim, naquele dia, 25.100 homens; todos estes puxavam [a] espada.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} derrotou Benjamim diante de Israel, e naquele dia os israelitas abateram 25.100 homens de Benjamim, todos eles armados de espada.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} deu a Israel a vitória sobre Benjamim. Naquele dia, os israelitas mataram 25.100 soldados de Benjamim, todos armados de espada.

decisions.choice: the LORD struck Benjamin: the victory is God's
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Benjamin used of Israel in verse 32. Now it is the LORD who strikes, as he promised in verse 28. The battle is told as his act first, and only then as Israel's.

decisions.choice: 25,100: a summary of the whole battle, told before the details
decisions.reason: This verse gives the result of the day. Verses 36-46 go back and tell how the battle went, step by step, ending with a round total of 25,000 (verse 46). On the size of the numbers see verse 2.

decisions.choice: defeated Benjamin before Israel (B); gave Israel victory over Benjamin (R)
decisions.reason: "Struck before" means defeated in front of, or for, Israel. Readable says plainly that God gave the victory.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֥וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִ֖ן כִּ֣י נִגָּ֑פוּ וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל מָקוֹם֙ לְבִנְיָמִ֔ן כִּ֤י בָֽטְחוּ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֹרֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁר שָׂ֖מוּ אֶל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] sons of Benjamin that they were struck down. And gave [the] men of Israel place to Benjamin, for they trusted in the ambush which they had set against the Gibeah.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin saw that they were struck down. And the men of Israel gave place to Benjamin, for they trusted in the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.
en.B: Then the Benjaminites saw that they were beaten. The men of Israel had given ground to Benjamin, because they were counting on the ambush they had set against Gibeah.
en.R: Then the men of Benjamin saw that they had lost. The Israelites had pulled back from them on purpose, because they were counting on the soldiers they had hidden near Gibeah.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakaona ya kuwa wamepigwa. Na watu wa Israeli walikuwa wamempa Benyamini nafasi, kwa maana waliwategemea wale waviziaji waliowaweka juu ya Gibea.
sw.B: Kisha Wabenyamini waliona kwamba wameshindwa. Watu wa Israeli walikuwa wamerudi nyuma mbele ya Benyamini, kwa sababu waliwategemea watu wa kuvizia waliowaweka dhidi ya Gibea.
sw.R: Kisha watu wa Benyamini waliona kwamba wameshindwa. Waisraeli walikuwa wamerudi nyuma mbele yao kwa makusudi, kwa sababu waliwategemea askari waliokuwa wamewaficha karibu na Gibea.

es.L: Y vieron los hijos de Benjamín que estaban derrotados. Y los hombres de Israel dieron lugar a Benjamín, porque confiaban en la emboscada que habían puesto contra Guibeá.
es.B: Entonces los benjamitas vieron que estaban derrotados. Los hombres de Israel habían cedido terreno ante Benjamín, porque contaban con la emboscada que habían puesto contra Guibeá.
es.R: Entonces los hombres de Benjamín vieron que habían perdido. Los israelitas se habían retirado a propósito, porque contaban con los soldados que habían escondido cerca de Guibeá.

fr.L: Et les fils de Benjamin virent qu’ils étaient battus. Et les hommes d’Israël avaient cédé du terrain à Benjamin, car ils comptaient sur l’embuscade qu’ils avaient placée contre Guibea.
fr.B: Les Benjaminites virent alors qu’ils étaient battus. Les hommes d’Israël avaient cédé du terrain à Benjamin, parce qu’ils comptaient sur l’embuscade qu’ils avaient tendue contre Guibea.
